newsitem.title: USA: US FERC okays Calif utilities' power market plan.
newsitem.headline: US FERC okays Calif utilities' power market plan.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Tuesday conditionally approved a plan by California's major utilities to set up a power market exchange and an independent system operator (ISO) to run their electricity transmission facilities.
The commission endorsed the broad outlines for setting up governing boards for an ISO and power exchange.
The commission said it would rule later on market power issues raised in the utilities' filing.
The commission rejected a California-only residency requirement which the utilities wanted for the two governing boards.

While not setting a minimum requirement for non-California residents, the commission said that in order for the governing board to be a truly regional independent system operator and power market, it should include at least some representatives from outside the state.
The commission set a March 31, 1997 deadline for the utilities to submit a second round of filings to answer a range of concerns.
The utilities were Pacific Gas and Electric Co, Edison International's Southern California Edison Co, and ENOVA Corp's San Diego Gas and Electric
